requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: A set expression SHALL NOT be an empty list.
requirements.original: An empty list and an empty negated list are not allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:negated-set-expression
requirements.canonical: A negated set expression SHALL NOT be an empty negated list.
requirements.original: An empty list and an empty negated list are not allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: A closing square bracket "]" immediately following an opening square bracket "[" SHALL be processed as a literal character.
requirements.original: Therefore a closing square bracket "]" immediately following an opening square bracket "[" or a caret following the opening square bracket "[" and immediately followed by a closing square bracket "]" shall be processed as literal characters.

requirements.subject: ent:negated-set-expression
requirements.canonical: A caret "^" following the opening square bracket "[" and immediately followed by a closing square bracket "]" SHALL be processed as a literal character, together with that "]".
requirements.original: Therefore a closing square bracket "]" immediately following an opening square bracket "[" or a caret following the opening square bracket "[" and immediately followed by a closing square bracket "]" shall be processed as literal characters.

ambiguity.issue: Unclear whether both "^" and the following "]" become literals (the list then continues) or only the "]". Chosen reading: both are literal, consistent with list item B.1.5.1-s024.
readings: In "[^]", both the caret and the closing bracket SHALL be processed as literal characters.
In "[^]", only the closing bracket SHALL be processed as a literal character and the caret keeps its negating meaning.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: Inside a set expression, every metacharacter except those listed in clause B.1.5.1 loses its special meaning.
requirements.original: All metacharacters, except those listed below, lose their special meaning inside the list:

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: Inside a set expression, "]" keeps its metacharacter meaning when it is not at the first position and does not immediately follow a "^" at the first position.
requirements.original: "]" not at the first position and not immediately following a "^" at the first position;

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-hyphen
requirements.canonical: Inside a set expression, "-" keeps its metacharacter meaning when it is not at the first or last position in the list.
requirements.original: "-" not at the first or last positions in the list;

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-caret
requirements.canonical: Inside a set expression, "^" keeps its metacharacter meaning when it is at the first position in the list and is not immediately followed by a closing square bracket.
requirements.original: "^" at the first position in the list except when immediately followed by a closing square bracket;

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: Inside a set expression, the metacharacters "\", "\d", "\t", "\w", "\r", "\n", "\s" and "\b" keep their metacharacter meaning.

ambiguity.issue: Meaning of the word-boundary metacharacter "\b" inside a set expression (which matches one character) is not defined.
readings: Inside a set expression, "\b" keeps its word-boundary meaning.
Inside a set expression, "\b" denotes some single character (e.g. backspace) rather than a word boundary.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-q
requirements.canonical: Inside a set expression, the metacharacter "\q{group,plane,row,cell}" keeps its metacharacter meaning.
requirements.original: "\q{group,plane,row,cell}";

ambiguity.issue: Only the quadruple form is listed; unclear whether the USI-like form \q{Uxxxx} also keeps its meaning inside a set expression.
readings: Inside a set expression, only the quadruple form of "\q" keeps its metacharacter meaning.
Inside a set expression, both the quadruple and the USI-like forms of "\q" keep their metacharacter meaning.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-n-reference
requirements.canonical: Inside a set expression, the metacharacter "\N{reference}" keeps its metacharacter meaning.
requirements.original: "\N{reference}".

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: An embedded set expression IS NOT allowed inside a set expression.
requirements.original: NOTE 1: Embedded lists are not allowed.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: In the pattern "[ab[r-z]]" the second "[" denotes a literal "[", the first "]" closes the set expression and the second "]" retains its literal value.
requirements.original: For example in pattern "[ab[r-z]]" the second "[" denotes a literal "[", the first "]" closes the list and the second "]" retains its literal value as no related opening bracket precedes it in the pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: The pattern "[ab[r-z]]" matches a two-character string whose first character is "a", "b", "[" or in the range "r"-"z" and whose second character is "]".
requirements.original: The pattern will match character strings containing two elements, with the first element equal to "a", "b", "[" or anything in the range "r"-"z" and the second character equal to "]".

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-caret
requirements.canonical: A literal caret "^" CAN be included in a set expression by placing it anywhere except the first position or by preceding it with a backslash.
requirements.original: NOTE 2: To include a literal caret character "^", place it anywhere except in the first position or precede it with a backslash.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-hyphen
requirements.canonical: A literal hyphen "-" CAN be included in a set expression by placing it first or last in the list or by preceding it with a backslash.
requirements.original: To include a literal hyphen "-", place it first or last in the list, or precede it with a backslash.

requirements.subject: ent:set-expression
requirements.canonical: A literal closing square bracket "]" CAN be included in a set expression by placing it first or by preceding it with a backslash.
requirements.original: To include a literal closing square bracket "]", place it first or precede it with a backslash.

requirements.subject: ent:negated-set-expression
requirements.condition: the first character in the set expression is "^"
requirements.canonical: If the first character in a set expression is the caret "^", the characters "-" and "]" match themselves when they immediately follow that caret.
requirements.original: If the first character in the list is the caret "^", then the characters "-" and "]" also match themselves when they immediately follow that caret.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expression
requirements.canonical: A character pattern MAY contain references to templates, constants, variables, formal parameters, module parameters, or fields of these, containing either a character string value or a pattern.
requirements.original: In addition to direct string values, it is also possible within the pattern to use references to templates, constants, variables, formal parameters, module parameters, or to their fields, containing either a character string value or pattern matching.

ambiguity.issue: "pattern matching" is used where a pattern (matching mechanism) is meant.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expression
requirements.canonical: A reference in a pattern SHALL be enclosed within the "{" and "}" characters.
requirements.original: The reference shall be enclosed within the "{" "}" characters and reference shall resolve a compatible character string type.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expression
requirements.canonical: A reference in a pattern SHALL resolve to a compatible character string type.
requirements.original: The reference shall be enclosed within the "{" "}" characters and reference shall resolve a compatible character string type.

ambiguity.issue: "compatible character string type" does not say compatible with what; chosen: compatible with the type of the pattern being constructed.
readings: A reference in a pattern SHALL resolve to an entity whose type is compatible with the character string type of the pattern being constructed.
A reference in a pattern SHALL resolve to an entity of any character string type (charstring or universal charstring).

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expression
requirements.canonical: The opening bracket "{" of a reference expression MAY be followed by a backslash.
requirements.original: The opening bracket can be optionally followed by a backslash.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-reference
requirements.condition: the opening bracket is not followed by a backslash
requirements.canonical: If the backslash is missing, the referenced character string or pattern SHALL be inserted into the pattern being constructed and SHALL be handled as a regular expression.
requirements.original: If the backslash character is missing, the referenced character string or pattern shall be inserted into the pattern being constructed and shall be handled as a regular expression.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expression
requirements.canonical: Each reference expression SHALL be dereferenced only once, before insertion; the dereferenced and inserted content SHALL NOT be dereferenced again.
requirements.original: Each expression shall be dereferenced only once, before the insertion (i.e. the expression dereferenced and inserted into the referencing pattern shall not be dereferenced again).

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-literal-reference
requirements.condition: the opening bracket is followed by a backslash
requirements.canonical: If the backslash is present, the referenced item SHALL contain a character string value.
requirements.original: If the backslash character is present, the referenced item shall contain a character string value in this case.

requirements.subject: ent:metachar-literal-reference
requirements.condition: the opening bracket is followed by a backslash
requirements.canonical: If the backslash is present, the referenced character string IS inserted into the pattern so that all its characters keep their literal value, i.e. all metacharacter symbols are automatically escaped.
requirements.original: The character string is inserted into the pattern being constructed so that it all characters contained in it can keep their literal value (i.e. all metacharacter symbols are automatically escaped).

requirements.subject: ent:ttcn3-tool
requirements.condition: the reference cannot be resolved or the referenced symbol does not fulfil the requirements
requirements.canonical: If a reference in a pattern cannot be resolved, or the referenced symbol does not fulfil the requirements of clause B.1.5.2, an error SHALL be generated.
requirements.original: If the reference cannot be resolved or if the referenced symbol does not fulfil the requirements set by this clause, an error shall be generated.

requirements.subject: ent:reference-expression
requirements.condition: the referenced definition or field contains reference expressions
requirements.canonical: If a referenced definition or field contains one or more reference expressions, those references SHALL be recursively dereferenced before its contents are inserted into the referencing pattern.
requirements.original: If a referenced definition or field of a definition contains one or more reference expressions, then these references shall recursively be dereferenced before inserting their contents into the referencing pattern.

requirements.subject: ent:pattern-fragment
requirements.condition: the pattern fragment contains a single reference only
requirements.canonical: If a pattern fragment contains a single reference only, the definition or field MAY be referenced directly, omitting the double quotes and the curly brackets.
requirements.original: If a fragment of a pattern contains a single reference only, it is allowed, as a shorthand notation, to reference the definition or the field of the definition directly, i.e. leave out double quotes (" ") and the pair of curly brackets ({ }).
